Picking where to go is half the fun, and choosing from the best track day circuits UK venues offer can feel overwhelming when you are starting out. Some tracks are wide, flowing and forgiving; others are narrow, blind and unforgiving of mistakes. Below I have ridden through the ten circuits that host the most motorcycle track days, with an honest note on each one's character, its signature corners and how kind it is to a nervous beginner.

Whatever you ride, from a friendly Kawasaki Ninja 650 to a full-fat Suzuki GSX-R1000R, there is a circuit here to suit your confidence.

What makes a great beginner circuit?

The friendliest tracks for a first-timer share a few traits: generous run-off so a mistake means a trip across grass rather than into a wall, good sightlines so you can see where the corner goes, and a rhythm that is easy to learn. Tight, blind or bumpy circuits reward local knowledge and can rattle a novice. None of the tracks below are off-limits to beginners, but some demand more respect than others. Before you book, weigh up:

  • Run-off. Wide gravel traps and grass verges turn a mistake into a scare rather than a crash.
  • Sightlines. Corners you can see into are far easier to commit to than blind, cresting ones.
  • Distance. A closer circuit means a relaxed arrival and more energy left for riding.
  • Cost. Shorter, older circuits are often cheaper and quieter midweek, which suits a first outing.
The best circuit for your first track day is rarely the most famous one. It is the one with the most run-off, the clearest lines and a novice group you can settle into. Save the intimidating ribbons of tarmac until you have a season under your belt.

Midlands and central circuits

Donington Park

Region: Leicestershire, East Midlands. Donington is the classic all-rounder and a superb first circuit. It flows beautifully, mixing the fast downhill plunge of Craner Curves with the technical Old Hairpin and the tight Melbourne loop. Signature corners are the Craner Curves and the Melbourne hairpin. Difficulty for beginners is low to moderate; the lines are logical and there is decent run-off, though Craner rewards commitment once you trust the bike.

Silverstone

Region: Northamptonshire. The home of British motorsport is wide, fast and smooth, with acres of run-off that make it reassuring despite the speeds. The flowing Maggotts and Becketts complex is its signature and one of the best sequences of corners in the world. Difficulty for beginners is low in terms of safety margin but the sheer size and speed can feel daunting; it is a great place to build confidence at your own pace.

Mallory Park

Region: Leicestershire. Short, old-school and characterful, Mallory is dominated by the long, fast Gerards sweep. It is compact and cheap, which makes it popular for first days, though the fast corners and limited run-off in places mean you should build up gently. Signature corner is Gerards. Difficulty for beginners is moderate.

South and east circuits

Brands Hatch

Region: Kent. Brands is a rollercoaster. The Indy circuit is short and intense, dropping into Paddock Hill Bend, a steep downhill right-hander that is thrilling and intimidating in equal measure. The longer GP loop adds fast, committed corners out in the countryside. Signature corner is Paddock Hill Bend. Difficulty for beginners is moderate to high; the gradients and blind crests demand respect.

Snetterton

Region: Norfolk. Flat, fast and flowing, Snetterton's 300 layout is a brilliant learning circuit with good visibility and run-off. The long Bentley straight leads into technical infield sections that teach you to link corners. Signature corners are Coram and the Bomb Hole. Difficulty for beginners is low to moderate.

Northern circuits

Oulton Park

Region: Cheshire. Many riders' favourite, Oulton is a stunning parkland circuit with dramatic elevation changes, from the plunge through Cascades to the climb over Hilltop. It is technical and rewarding but the changes in gradient and camber make it one to learn carefully. Signature corners are Cascades and Druids. Difficulty for beginners is moderate to high.

Cadwell Park

Region: Lincolnshire. The Mountain circuit is narrow, twisty and hilly, famously featuring the Mountain jump where bikes can get airborne. It is enormous fun but tight and blind in places with limited run-off, so it is best tackled once you have a few days under your belt. Signature feature is the Mountain. Difficulty for beginners is high.

Croft

Region: North Yorkshire. A fast, flowing circuit with a good mix of quick sweeps and a tight chicane complex. It is relatively wide and well-sighted, making it a solid choice as you step up your pace. Signature corner is the Jim Clark esses. Difficulty for beginners is low to moderate.

Scotland and Wales

Knockhill

Region: Fife, Scotland. Scotland's national circuit is short, hilly and undulating, packing a lot of character into a small footprint. The gradients keep you busy and the surface has real character. Signature corner is the Duffus Dip. Difficulty for beginners is moderate; the constant elevation change takes learning.

Anglesey

Region: North Wales. Possibly the most spectacular setting in Britain, the Coastal circuit runs along the Irish Sea with breathtaking views. It is flowing, technical and superbly surfaced, with the fast Rocket corner and the Corkscrew descent as highlights. Difficulty for beginners is moderate, and the trip is worth every mile.

Which circuit should a beginner choose?

If I had to send a first-timer anywhere, I would point them at Donington Park, Silverstone or Snetterton for their generous run-off and logical lines. Save Cadwell and Brands Hatch until you have learned to read a circuit. Before you book, read our beginner's guide to motorcycle track days so you know what to expect on the day, and sort your kit with our track day gear checklist. If you would rather chase the perfect corner on public roads, our pick of the best roads for sportsbikes UK riders love is a great place to start, and a sport-tourer like the Suzuki GSX-S1000GT will happily do both.

Save intimidating tracks like Cadwell Park (the Mountain) and Brands Hatch (Paddock Hill Bend) until you have a season under your belt.
Circuit character varies hugely, from Silverstone's fast, wide sweeps to Oulton Park's dramatic parkland elevation changes.
Consider run-off, sightlines, distance and cost before booking, as shorter older circuits are often cheaper and quieter midweek.
Anglesey's Coastal circuit is possibly Britain's most spectacular setting, running right along the Irish Sea.

faq.q: Which UK circuit is best for a first track day?
faq.a: Donington Park, Silverstone and Snetterton are the top picks for first-timers thanks to their generous run-off and logical lines. Donington flows beautifully and its lines are easy to read, Silverstone is wide and smooth with acres of run-off, and Snetterton's 300 layout has good visibility and space. Save Cadwell and Brands Hatch until you can read a circuit.

faq.q: Which circuits should beginners avoid at first?
faq.a: Cadwell Park's Mountain circuit is narrow, twisty and hilly, with the famous Mountain jump where bikes get airborne, and it has limited run-off, so it rates as high difficulty. Brands Hatch is a rollercoaster whose gradients and blind crests around Paddock Hill Bend demand respect. Both are best tackled once you have a few days of experience.

The friendliest tracks share generous run-off so a mistake means a trip across grass rather than into a wall, good sightlines so you can see where a corner goes, and a rhythm that is easy to learn. Tight, blind or bumpy circuits reward local knowledge and can rattle a novice, so choose an open, well-sighted track for your first outing.

faq.q: How should I choose which circuit to book?
faq.a: Weigh up four things before booking: run-off, since wide gravel traps turn a mistake into a scare rather than a crash; sightlines, as corners you can see into are easier to commit to; distance, because a closer circuit means a relaxed arrival; and cost, as shorter, older circuits are often cheaper and quieter midweek, which suits a first outing.

faq.q: Which circuit has the best setting?
faq.a: Anglesey in North Wales has possibly the most spectacular setting in Britain, with the Coastal circuit running along the Irish Sea and breathtaking views. It is flowing, technical and superbly surfaced, with the fast Rocket corner and the Corkscrew descent as highlights, and it rates as moderate difficulty for beginners. The trip is worth every mile.
